text:
maria: hey all — small WFH PSA: my ficus apparently decided it likes sitting on the router. wifi has been flaking out all morning, pics attached. anyone tried plant-based network troubleshooting? :seedling: :wifi:
jamal: 😂 unplug it? plants are not supported hardware. did you try power-cycling the modem + router yet?
maria: yep tried unplug for 30s. no joy. sometimes the downstairs neighbor loses it too so might be ISP hiccups. isp status site shows intermittent degraded performance.
alex: have you tried switching the router to 5GHz or moving the channel? also check for overheating if it's getting direct sun on the router.
maria: good call — i moved the router off the windowsill and turned 5GHz on. small improvement but still spikes. here's a quick ping run to google:
```
PING 8.8.8.8 (8.8.8.8): 56 data bytes
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=0 ttl=118 time=25.1 ms
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=1 ttl=118 time=240.3 ms
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=2 ttl=118 time=28.4 ms
--- 8.8.8.8 ping statistics ---
3 packets transmitted, 3 packets received, 0.0% packet loss
rtt min/avg/max = 25.1/97.9/240.3 ms
```
lina: ouch that max is spicy. could be microbursts on the last-mile. if neighbor has same, call ISP and ask for line check. also: put a coaster under the router for airflow and away from the ficus roots :sweat_smile:
sean: if you want a cheap immediate fix, a wifi powerline + mini travel router can bypass flaky AP placement issues. otherwise mesh helps. got one for $40 that saved my sanity last year.
maria: thanks! gonna call ISP after lunch and try powerline tonight. also proudly relocating plant — new desk corner for the ficus. pic of plant throne -> no more router nap.
ops-bot: note: office network team reminder — home setups vary; if you need a temporary hotspot from the company while troubleshooting, ping @it-support in #help.
jamal: also, tip: run a 1-hour continuous ping to a stable IP to capture when spikes happen and include timestamps when opening a ticket. helps them correlate.
maria: will do. thanks everyone — and sorry team, no more plant/devops experiments on network gear from now on :raised_hands:
alex: gif: tiny ficus with ethernet cable :laughing:
lina: :thumbsup:
